meta_title: Not an OroCommerce Alternative: Keep It, Add Voice Ordering
meta_desc: OroCommerce suits corporate buying. Chefs who skip the store can say a short reorder into our app and check it. Not an OroCommerce alternative: keep it.

hero.h1: Not An OroCommerce Alternative: No Login To Reorder
hero.lead: When a chef would rather phone than sign in to your store, let them send each short reorder as a list they have looked over. In the VoiceOrder Solutions app, chefs say their usual items and fix any wrong one before sending. OroCommerce keeps the storefront, sign-offs and quotes your larger accounts use.

stats.label: Saved on each reorder sent in the app, not by phone

problem.h2: What has distributors searching for an OroCommerce competitor
problem.lead: OroCommerce does its best work with corporate buyers, while a restaurant reorder is often one chef with a short list, so some of those chefs still call. Swapping in an OroCommerce alternative would not end that call. Orders from our app skip the store. If you have them emailed, your team types each one in from the chef's own checked list.

cards.body: Oro describes its platform as designed for corporate accounts and complex workflows: account hierarchies, roles and permissions, approval chains, budgets and quotes. A chef topping up produce and dairy for the weekend needs none of it.

cards.h3: Oro says it too: plenty of buyers prefer a call
cards.body: Oro's own AI page says many buyers still prefer sending orders or calling their rep to navigating a portal. Each of those calls means someone at your desk listening and typing every item into your system.

cards.h3: Oro's voice assistant is for signed-in buyers
cards.body: SmartAgent, Oro's buyer assistant, takes spoken or typed requests from people signed in to your Enterprise store. A chef in the habit of calling your rep may never open it, and that reorder still comes by phone.

features.h2: Not an OroCommerce alternative: what it adds for the quick reorder

rows.h3: A short reorder, with no store to open
rows.body: Standing at the walk-in, the chef names what is running low. Our app matches each spoken item to the restaurant's own guide and lists them, so the chef can change an item or an amount before sending.
bullets: Each item sits on the chef's screen until they press send
A reorder can still go in after close or on a holiday
Runs on the chef's own iOS or Android phone
Saves 20 to 30 minutes compared with the same order by phone
If the chef gets pulled away, the order is saved where they stopped

link.text: How restaurants get their orders to you →

rows.h3: Its own guide for every restaurant you supply
rows.body: Send us what each restaurant normally orders, with prices; an export from your store or ERP is typical. We turn it into the guide that restaurant orders from. You update each account's guide and prices in our admin platform, where you also manage the accounts. Whether price changes can come over from OroCommerce or your ERP in bulk is a question for the demo.
bullets: Every item carries your own item number
Guide changes are yours to make, one account at a time, in our admin
Setup works from a spreadsheet, with no OroCommerce login
Nothing in your store's catalogs changes

rows.h3: Delivered to the inbox or system you choose
rows.body: We send each finished order to you as an email attachment, or by EDI, our API or QuickBooks. It never passes through your OroCommerce storefront, so it will not show in the store's order history unless your setup loads it there. An EDI or API order can land in your ERP or OroCommerce directly if your setup is built for it; a demo tells you whether it can. A QuickBooks order goes to your books, not into OroCommerce.
bullets: Sent to one rep or to a shared order desk address
Over EDI or the API, when your setup takes it, nobody retypes it
Your team enters emailed orders from the chef's approved list
Picking and delivery carry on as they run now

rows.h3: Stock in view alongside the reorders
rows.body: VoiceOrder Solutions gives you real-time inventory visibility tied to order activity. It does not replace your stock system: that stays in charge, and a demo shows how the levels connect.
bullets: Stock shown to buyers in your store is left as it is
Fewer stockout surprises for whoever takes orders
Stock numbers come from the system you count with today
Buying from your own suppliers stays in your ERP

cards.h2: What OroCommerce keeps doing, and what we take on
cards.lead: We are not an alternative to OroCommerce: our one job is moving a restaurant's short reorder from its chef to you.

items.body: We set up only the restaurants you list, so an account happy with the store keeps using it, with its approvals and payments.
Quote requests, and the field sales app reps use to build quotes on site, stay in OroCommerce. Our app is for the reorder itself, from a chef who already knows what to restock.
If buyers use SmartAgent in your store, or SmartOrder drafts the purchase orders customers email you, keep both running. Ours is a separate app that the chef holds.

midcta.h3: Hear one reorder said, corrected and sent
midcta.body: In a 20-minute demo, you watch us say a sample reorder into the app, replace one product with another, send it, then see what lands on your desk. Then we cover how it would sit beside the store you run on OroCommerce.

steps.lead: You send the regular items for each account, we set up each restaurant on our side, and the chef puts the app on their phone.

items.body: A spreadsheet listing each restaurant's normal items with their prices, under your codes, is usually all we need.
We load its guide, then the chef downloads the app and can order from that guide.
Orders from the app each carry a number and a send time, in the format you set up.

faq.h2: Questions distributors running OroCommerce bring us

items.q: Do we need an OroCommerce alternative before chefs can reorder by voice?
items.a: No. Your storefront, catalogs and approval rules stay as they are. The change is for a restaurant whose chef calls your desk today: that chef now says the reorder aloud in our app and goes over every item before it reaches you.

items.q: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than OroCommerce?
items.a: Only at one narrow job: a short restaurant reorder from a chef happier saying it than shopping for it. OroCommerce does far more, from corporate accounts to payments, so we run alongside it and are not an OroCommerce alternative.

items.q: Oro's SmartAgent already accepts voice. What does your app add?
items.a: It is a real overlap. On the Enterprise edition, a buyer signed in to your store can ask SmartAgent, by voice or in writing, to check stock or place a reorder. If restaurants on your store use SmartAgent, keep it. Ours is a separate phone app built only around each restaurant's regular items: the chef just talks, then looks over what the app lists and fixes anything wrong before it goes, with no storefront to open.

items.q: Is it linked to OroCommerce? Will someone here still type these orders?
items.a: The two are separate, nothing joins them out of the box, and you get support for each from its own company. By email, your office receives a file of the reorder as sent, so nobody answers a call, notes it down and reads it back; someone enters it from a finished list the chef approved. Through EDI or the API, it may load into OroCommerce or your ERP without retyping, provided either system is built to take such orders, which we check together in the demo. OroCommerce runs the store, and your ERP remains the system of record for customer accounts, inventory and billing. Our side holds the order guide for every restaurant, with its prices, plus the reorders that come through the app. A chef who phones instead still gets no order number from us.

items.q: Some of our customers are groups with approval rules. Does this change that?
items.a: No. Groups that need sign-offs, budgets and several logins keep ordering in OroCommerce, where those rules live. We made our app for the restaurant where the chef decides what to order and sends it.

items.q: Is OroCommerce a fit for foodservice distributors at all?
items.a: It can be. Oro sells to many kinds of distributors, and food distributors run it: one family-owned foodservice distributor in Ohio had an integrator add order guides and cut-off times for its restaurant customers. If your store works for the accounts on it, keep it, and add us for chefs who prefer the phone.

items.q: How soon can we start, and how is pricing set?
items.a: Setup is 24 to 48 hours for most distributors, with nothing in OroCommerce touched. You give us the items each restaurant tends to buy, most often in a spreadsheet exported from your system. From that we build the guides in our admin, then open an account for every restaurant. Each chef adds the app to their phone, and at most restaurants the first reorder goes out that same day. Oro explains that its license is priced on the value of goods sold through the store and offers a free Community Edition, but quotes its Enterprise pricing; we quote ours for each distributor too. An OroCommerce replacement would mean building a new store, which Oro's own FAQ puts at about six months on average, while adding us keeps yours as it is.

items.q: Where do the OroCommerce details on this page come from?
items.a: From oroinc.com, as we found it on 9 November 2026: the homepage, its FAQ, pricing, product, distributors, portal, workflow, AI and consumer-goods pages, plus Oro's documentation on its AI features and an integrator's case study of a foodservice company. If anything here no longer matches their site, tell us and we will correct it.

mainCta.h2: Sign-offs for the groups who need them. Quick spoken reorders for chefs who need none.
mainCta.body: Give us twenty minutes to show a reorder going from the walk-in to your desk, the way a chef who skips your store would send it.
